asof: Settles Tue 27 Oct 2026 · written Wed 28 Oct
headline: A confidence beat lifts SR3's 2027 hikes again into the FOMC; U7 peaks at 4.69%, well past consensus. Fade still on, near its stop.
summary: The strip sold off for a second day, again led by 2027: implied rates rose 3–4bp from H7 to H8, with U7 and Z7 up 4bp, while Z6 was unchanged at 4.20% and U6 eased 0.7bp. Over two sessions M7 and U7 are 8bp higher in rate, trimming October's rally to 16.4bp and 18.5bp, and Z7 is 21.2bp lower than at the end-September (modelled) settle. The peak is SR3U7 at 4.69%, 76bp above the latest 3.93% SOFR fixing, with 19.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. Consensus remains one or two more hikes: all 100 Reuters economists see December, and about 60% see the cycle ending at 4.00–4.25%.
drivers: The Conference Board index jumped 7.5 points to 91.7, the highest since June, against forecasts near 80–81, with the present-situation gauge up 8.6 to 120.4 and the jobs differential up 2.4 points. A firmer consumer on the eve of the FOMC is what pushed H7–U7 3–4bp higher.
Five-year auction was solid, not enough to rally

The $70bn 5-year cleared at 4.845% (0.3bp tail) with a 2.33 bid-to-cover against a 2.31 average and indirects at 60% (54% last time), well below September's 5.033% stop. The 2-year still edged up about 1bp to near 4.72%, so supply was not the source of the selloff; the $30bn FRN (Wed) and $44bn 7-year (Thu) remain.
FOMC positioning: hold, with hawks heard

Previews line up behind a hold on Wednesday and a December hike: Goldman sees a hike every other meeting, ING a December move then a long pause, and Rabobank and ING flag possible hike dissents from Hammack, Kashkari and Logan. Fed funds futures carried 12% odds of a move on Wednesday at Monday's close.

Brent settled $1.93 lower at $113.88 and WTI back under $100 at $99.90 on diplomacy headlines, which did not help 2027 contracts. SOFR printed 3.93% for 26 October, 5bp over EFFR (3.88%) and above IORB (3.90%), with the 99th percentile at 4.01%; the FHLBNY flags Canadian year-end and MBS paydowns on 30 October as the next test.
spreads: The whites steepened again as 2027 sold off and December held: U6/Z6 +26.7bp (+0.7bp on the day), Z6/H7 +28bp (+3bp, +5bp on the week) and H7/M7 +16bp (+0.5bp), with M7/U7 at +5bp and U7/Z7 flat at −2.5bp. Z6/Z7 widened 4bp to +46.5bp and Z6/M7 3.5bp to +44bp, though both remain narrower month to date (−11.2bp and −6.4bp). The flies were steady: H7/M7/U7 at +11bp (flat) and M7/U7/Z7 at +7.5bp (+0.5bp). Beyond the peak the reds and greens inverted further because the 2029 contracts lagged: Z7/Z8 −11bp (−1.5bp), U7/Z8 −13.5bp (−1.5bp, −4.5bp on the week) and Z8/Z9 −6bp (−1bp); the 2028–29 settle history starts 22 October, so there is no month-to-date base.
fed: Fed funds futures, last recorded at Monday's close, price 3bp for Wednesday (12% odds of a hike), 22.7bp cumulative by December (81% chance of at least one hike), 48.6bp by March, 66.8bp by June and a 73bp peak at the September 2027 FOMC (implied EFFR 4.61%). That is up from 21.5bp, 43.9bp and 68.5bp at Friday's close, but still below a week ago (26.3bp by December, 55.2bp by March, 78bp peak) and well below end-September (30.6bp, 63.4bp and a 94bp peak). SR3 is consistent: U7 at 4.69% sits 8bp over the ZQ peak, about 5bp of it the SOFR–EFFR basis and the rest Tuesday's 4bp selloff, which ZQ has not yet recorded. Against that, 94 of 100 Reuters economists see a hold this week, all 100 a December hike and roughly 60% a 4.00–4.25% peak, while 12 of 18 September projections showed one more hike this year; the market still carries close to 50bp of 2027 tightening that most forecasters do not.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 6bp against at +44bp after two 2027-led selloffs, 4bp from the stop, but still 6.4bp narrower than at end-September. Nothing in the confidence beat changes the case: Z6 holds the December hike everyone expects, while M7 carries a second and third hike neither the dots nor most economists project. Levels unchanged; the FOMC is the test, and a hold without hiking guidance should let M7 recover.
ideas.risk: Hike dissents or a Warsh nod to faster tightening would widen the spread through the +48bp stop.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open and 3bp in favour at −11bp: Tuesday's selloff hit Z7 (+4bp) more than Z8 (+2.5bp), so the hedge again offset part of the core's loss. If the Fed takes SOFR toward 4.7% with Brent above $110, the easing that follows is likely larger than the 19.5bp now priced from the U7 peak to Z9. Keep at about half the core size.
ideas.risk: A 'higher for longer' plateau through 2028 with no cuts would push the spread back toward flat.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: About 45% of U6's quarter is now fixed and SOFR printed 3.93%, 5bp over EFFR, so firmer month-end funding can only cost a long, while only 3bp of a hike is priced for Wednesday. U6 eased 0.7bp on Tuesday and is just 0.2bp lower on the week; revisit after the FOMC and the 30 October and 2 November prints.
ideas.risk: A surprise hike on Wednesday would cost U6 roughly 10bp; a dovish surprise would lift it only a few bp.

watch: FOMC decision, Warsh press conference; $30bn 2-year FRN
Hold expected (3bp priced); hike dissents would firm December and test the core trade's stop.
Core PCE seen near 3.1% y/y and GDP near 3%; a hot core print lifts H7–U7.
Q3 employment cost index, Chicago PMI, month-end
ECI seen at 0.7–0.8%; Canadian year-end and MBS paydowns test SOFR's 3.93% print.
Prices paid was 77.9 in September; $213bn of notes settle the same day.
Fiscal outlook and term premium; mostly a red/green contract story.
September added only 29,000; another soft report would revive the 2027 rally.
Brent at $113.88 remains the main risk to fading 2027 hikes; $120 is the pain point.
